plain.text: Jesus looked toward heaven and prayed: "Father, the hour has come. Glorify your Son, that your Son may glorify you." The Father had given him authority to give eternal life. "Now this is eternal life: that they know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom you have sent." He had finished the work the Father gave him, and asked to share again the glory he had before the world began.

Jesus prayed for his disciples. "I have revealed you to those you gave me. They have obeyed your word." He was leaving the world, but they were staying. "Holy Father, protect them by the power of your name, so that they may be one as we are one." He did not ask that they be taken out of the world, but protected from the evil one. "Sanctify them by the truth; your word is truth. As you sent me into the world, I have sent them into the world."

"My prayer is not for them alone. I pray also for those who will believe in me through their message, that all of them may be one, Father, just as you are in me and I am in you. May they also be in us, so that the world may believe that you have sent me." He prayed that they would be with him and see his glory, and that the love the Father has for him would be in them.

summary.bigIdea: Before his death, Jesus prays for his glory, for his disciples' protection and unity, and for all future believers.
points: "This is eternal life: that they know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ."
Jesus prays that his followers will be protected and sent into the world.
He prays for all believers to be one, so the world may believe.
summary.reflection: Jesus prayed for those who would believe in the future, which includes believers today. How does it feel to know you were in his prayer?
